correctness.rationale: The exact generator gives \(s[s^{-G}-1]=\exp(s\log s)-s\to1\), so its Weibull-flexible exponent is asymptotic to \(s^{-\alpha}\). The outer Type-I transform contributes only the factor \(\lambda\) to the leading negative log survival, because its denominator converges to \(\lambda\). The Burr XII, quantile, heavy-tail and moment conclusions then follow from elementary regular-variation and exponential-comparison arguments. The Weibull-baseline conclusion follows by direct substitution. A standalone numerical checker evaluates the exact formulas only as a consistency test.

value.rationale: Tail heaviness is a headline modeling motivation of the target family and directly underlies its actuarial-risk discussion. The result supplies a baseline-invariant structural tail theorem, gives an exact Burr XII parameter phase boundary, makes the extreme-quantile scale explicit, and shows that the Weibull-baseline special case is asymptotically lighter than every exponential. It also preserves the paper's displayed Burr XII risk example by verifying that its parameters lie in the genuine heavy-tail region. This is a natural complete classification, not a plot-based or arbitrary parameter-slice observation.
